title: Kiln Omnichain POC — Hybrid edge/core latency & cost deep dive (working notes)
body:
Summary:
Working notes from the Kiln Omnichain customer POC workshop focused on hybrid edge/core deployments. Objective: validate that a mixed topology (local edge inference for short-form interactions + regional core GPUs for long context / high-quality results) can hit 200ms median for common flows while keeping incremental inference cost under $10k/mo for pilot traffic (avg 200k UA/month).

Who attended:
- Kiln eng leads (demo + traffic profile)
- Redwood solutions (Amina, Carlos, Rina) and infra support (Noah)

Test harness + methodology (quick):
- Traffic shape: sampled production traces from Kiln (retail order flows + chat support searches). Synthetic microburst scenarios added: 1000 concurrent short requests arriving over 1s, and 10k QPS synthetic ramp.
- Models evaluated: redwood-7b (fp16), redwood-13b-quant (gptq 4-bit), llama2-13b-vanilla (baseline), small-edge-onnx (4-bit, CPU fallback).
- Hardware: edge node = c6g + Intel AVX512 CPU with ONNX runtime; edge accel test w/ Jetson-like ARM device simulated. Core pool = H100 (region-a), A100-80GB (region-b). Dedicated pool with reserved capacity vs. hosted route tested.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end response time, throughput (concurrent QPS sustained), cold-start (container spinup) and warm-start, cost per 1M tokens, cost per 10k requests, and tail-spike behavior under burst.

Key observations (raw):
- Short-form responses (<= 32 tokens):
  - Edge small-edge-onnx: p50 ~28ms, p95 ~90ms, p99 ~220ms (CPU-only; good for tiny replies)
  - Core redwood-7b (batched): p50 ~45ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~420ms
  - Core redwood-13b-quant (batched, H100): p50 ~60ms, p95 ~220ms, p99 ~620ms
  - Tail amplification during microbursts is driven by queueing at the core; observed p99 spikes ~3-6x baseline when concurrent queue > 200

- Long-form / high-quality (>= 256 tokens):
  - redwood-13b-quant on H100: median per-token latency comparable to 7b per-token but total response time larger due to token count (expected).
  - Cost per full response (avg 320 tokens): 13b-quant ~ $0.012/response; 7b ~ $0.007/response (approx., includes GPU infra amortized).

- Cold start:
  - Edge container cold start (onnx): < 500ms when already warmed by host OS; full process cold boot (edge device reboot) much higher and unacceptable for interactive SLA.
  - Core GPU cold start (new replica spinup): 8–14s depending on image layers and cold KV cache; careful pre-warm required for interactive SLOs.

- Batching and throughput sensitivity:
  - Increasing batch_size from 1->8 improved throughput ~3.5x but increased median per-request latency by ~20–40ms. For Kiln use-case (interactive), we found batch_size 2–4 was sweet spot if latency SLO is 200ms.
  - Adaptive batching (latency target based) helped reduce cost by ~18% vs fixed small batches during off-peak without violating p95 targets.

- Caching (KV prefix + full response cache):
  - Prefix KV cache (warm) cut token generation time by ~35% on median for repeat queries; effective for short repetitive prompts (search suggestions).
  - Response-level cache for deterministic calls (e.g., templated re-ranks) reduced core load by up to 40% during promo spikes.

- Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
  - When core capacity reached >90% util, fallback to edge small model (lower quality) kept tail latency bounded but quality regressions were visible. Need explicit fallback policy and automatic tagging of degraded responses.

Cost sensitivity and numbers (pilot scale approx):
- Baseline: mixed routing (30% edge, 70% core) with reserved core A100 pool (sustained)
  - Monthly infra cost (pilot estimate): $6.5k (core reserved amortized) + $1.2k (edge infra) + $0.8k networking = ~$8.5k/mo
  - Per-1M token cost (inference only): ~ $22 (includes batching amortization and KV/cache hit assumptions)
- If move to hosted-only redwood-13b-quant for all requests (no edge): cost increases by ~2.1x, tail latency slightly lower median but higher p99 under bursts unless we add burst capacity.

Actionable recommendations for Kiln POC:
1) Hybrid routing config: keep short-form flows pinned to edge models (auto-detect by token_count <=32 or prompt tag). Route longer contexts to core redwood-13b-quant.
2) Pre-warm policy: maintain min_replicas=2 in core pool during business hours; add predictive warmups based on traffic signals (cron + observed lead indicators).
3) Batching: use adaptive batching with max_batch=8, latency_target=120ms for the core pool. Set prefer_latency_for_routes for checkout flows.
4) Caching: enable prefix KV cache for search/autocomplete with TTL=120s; enable response-level cache for templated reranks (ttl=60s).
5) Fallbacks: implement model_fallback policy chain: redwood-13b-quant -> redwood-7b -> small-edge-onnx (with degrade_tag metadata). Surface degrade_tag to client for telemetry.
6) Observability: add synthetic canary that exercises tails (microburst generator) every 10m; create dashboard with p50/p95/p99, queue_length, batch_size histograms, KV cache hit ratio, and cost burn rate.

Open questions / risks:
- Edge hardware variance: Kiln's planned edge devices have CPU variance; need lab sweep with actual target devices (we simulated).
- Network egress costs if routing many long responses from core to edge will bump monthly bill; quantify with real telemetry.
- Quality delta for fallback chain: we should run A/B with human eval for degraded flows to measure UX impact.

Next steps / owners:
- Lab sweep on Kiln's sample edge device images (Carlos) — run microburst and cold start profile by 2030-03-26.
- Implement adaptive batching prototype in dev cluster and run 48h soak (Rina) — target 2030-04-02.
- Add canary microburst generator and dashboard tile (Noah) — target 2030-03-28.
- Draft deployment proposal with recommended cost projections / SLA edits for Kiln (Amina) — target 2030-04-05.

Notes / random observations:
- Observed a weird p99 amplification when KV cache eviction coincided with a 1s microburst (likely cache stampede). Mitigation: jittered TTLs and randomized prefetch.
- For very short interactions (chat suggestions) latency dominated by network hop on region <-> edge; consider local embedding match on edge for re-rank first-pass.

Appendix (quick experiment logs):
- run-2030-03-14-edge-cpu-onnx.log: median 28ms, 99th 220ms
- run-2030-03-15-core-h100-batch-4.log: p95 220ms, p99 610ms, avg batch 3.1
- cost-sim-2030-03-18.csv: includes amortized reserved vs on-demand scenarios (see linked artifacts)

If helpful we can turn this into a short recommendations one-pager for Kiln execs (separate final doc). For now this is a working capture of measurements, hypotheses, and next steps.

-- Amina
